scope: Read-only official implementation audit; no Android fault injection, package install, Dart/Flutter execution or product change was performed for this audit.

official_android_plugin.binding_limit: Official version-tag source was read and hashed; the pub.dev archive was not downloaded or compared.

android_framework.scope_limit: Official AOSP Android 15 source. The current emulator/framework binary and Android 17 implementation were not disassembled or fault-injected.

findings.evidence: SharedPreferencesAndroid.registerWith sets SharedPreferencesStorePlatform.instance to SharedPreferencesAndroid; main Kotlin plugin also attaches LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.
findings.conclusion: The old getInstance API reaches legacy Android SharedPreferences, not the separately registered async DataStore backend.

findings.evidence: LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.kt 56–66 returns Editor.putString(...).commit(); Dart setValue 43–46 forwards that boolean.
findings.conclusion: The adapter receives the native commit result. A true result is the Android API's positive persistent-storage acknowledgement, not a synthetic Dart-cache success.

findings.evidence: Dart shared_preferences_legacy.dart 223–227 replaces its cache after platform getAll; LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.kt 104–115 reads preferences.all; AOSP 297–301 returns a copy of mMap.
findings.conclusion: Successful reload refreshes the Dart cache from native memory. It is not an independent disk read.

findings.evidence: AOSP commit 610 calls commitToMemory; line580 updates the map. Later failure branches789/808 report false without rolling back that map. Host memory_round.dart 245/281–284/354 accepts equal readback after a failed write.
findings.conclusion: Under an actual native commit failure after memory mutation, round or stats could be accepted as saved solely because reload observes the native optimistic cache. This source path is proven; an actual Android disk failure has not been reproduced.

findings.evidence: AOSP same-value skip575–577 does not advance memory generation, but synchronous writeToFile759–776 writes when disk generation is behind. Commit610–626 waits for its disk result.
findings.conclusion: A separately successful same-value setString can provide a new positive platform acknowledgement. Read equality alone cannot. This does not establish hardware/fsync or cross-engine compare-and-swap guarantees.

tests.existing_14_boundary: The prior 14 Dart-cache cases use an InMemory platform backend whose before-commit faults do not optimistically change a separate native memory map. Their observed PASS remains valid for that stated boundary, not for this newly audited native-cache path.
